$comment: Sail motion preset vocabulary — a CLOSED, design-system-owned set of spring + tween configs. The compiler resolves a `motion: { scale: 'sm' }` reference against this file at build time. Adding a preset = adding a row here + (optionally) extending the sx token surface. Mirrors the `sail-sx` rule's design: token-only, no raw values, no bracket escape.

spring:snappy.$doc: high-stiffness, well-damped — quick UI feedback (button press, toggle)

spring:gentle.$doc: softer settling — hover state, panel expand

spring:bouncy.$doc: visible overshoot — playful micro-interaction, badge pop

spring:deliberate.$doc: slow, weighty — page transitions, drawer slide

press.$doc: scale-down on pointerdown — paired with a spring:snappy release

release.$doc: scale-up on pointerup — completes the press/release pair

pulse.$doc: gentle scale pulse, infinite — loading state, attention

bounce.$doc: translateY 0→-100% + opacity 0.4→1 — a 7-12px dot's visible bounce, paired per dot, with a 150ms stagger step that lands as a per-dot phase offset (dot 1: 0ms, dot 2: 150ms, dot 3: 300ms).

marquee.$doc: translateX 0→-50% — the <sail-band> one-direction infinite loop. The runtime derives the duration from measured content width (px/s), so the rate holds for any content. Use `marquee-reverse` to flip direction.

marquee-reverse.$doc: translateX 0→+50% — the <sail-band direction="reverse"> one-direction loop. Same px/s derivation as `marquee`.

property_aliases.$doc: Property values for `motion: { scale: 'sm' }` — the agent picks a scale alias, the compiler resolves to (0.96/1.02/1.06/...). Mirrors how `sx="text:sm"` resolves to `var(--text-sm)`.
